subject: tuned mass damper
title: What If a 660-Ton Steel Ball Hung Inside a Skyscraper? Taipei 101 Has One

scenes.text: What if you hung a 660-ton steel ball inside a skyscraper? One tower did, to survive typhoons.
Taipei 101 stands 508 metres tall in a city of earthquakes and typhoons. Tall towers sway, and the people inside feel seasick.
So between floors 87 and 92 hangs a gold sphere, 18 feet across, on steel cables. The biggest tuned mass damper on Earth.
When wind pushes the tower one way, the ball lags and swings the other, pulling it back. Pistons soak up the energy.
In August 2015, Typhoon Soudelor hit with gusts over 100 miles an hour. The ball swung a full metre, the most ever recorded.
In 2024, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake shook Taiwan. Cameras caught the ball swinging. The tower stood. Visitors now pay to watch it.

description:
What if a 660-ton steel ball hung inside a skyscraper? Taipei 101 has one: the largest tuned mass damper in the world, suspended between the 87th and 92nd floors of the 508-metre tower.
The sphere swings against the building's motion, and pistons absorb the energy, cutting the sway from wind and earthquakes. During Typhoon Soudelor in August 2015, with winds around 100 mph, the ball moved a record 1 metre.

first_comment: Dampers in skyscrapers usually weigh 300 to 800 tons; without one, a tall tower in a typhoon can sway far enough to make people seasick. Which piece of hidden engineering should we run through next?
